scope: Source review of the existing QuorumTest#testMultiToFollower and previously tested request-receive-context overlay. This is not an exhaustive exclusion of other tests or fault models.

source_evidence.finding: Three-peer test connects a client to a follower, submits one multi-create request, reads three nodes, and closes. It has no explicit application request retry or peer restart.

The physical REQUEST read precedes Request creation and submitLearnerRequest; an IOException at the read exits through the outer handler and closes the socket, so that packet does not reach the selected target.

The processor claims then processes each Request; an exception escaping before pRequest exits its loop. For createSession, trackSession and setOwner are adjacent with no I/O between. For multi-create, checkSession is reached in pRequest2Txn; no new caught precheck I/O door was identified in this inspected path.
ZOOKEEPER-02 checkSession depends on the session's owner identity; ZOOKEEPER-03 setOwner throws only for an absent or closing session.

The existing connect-read door precedes session creation/renewal, so its exception drops that connection attempt. The locally caught readBool IOException only changes old-client/read-only handling; it does not change the selected session owner or existence operands.

decision.reason: The existing healthy exact packet and actor path is valid, but the previously tested faults did not preserve a time-respecting path from the affected request to the selected target. No distinct source-supported target-retaining request receive or processor-claim exception point was found in this review.
